Lessons.Title: Interpret Remainders in Division Situations
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Represent division in situations with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors. Interpret the quotient and any remainder based on what the numbers mean, not by a mechanical rule.
2021 source sequence: Choral Count (multiples of 2, 3 and 5); Muffins and Seats; Save for a Garden and a student-invented division situation; Lesson Synthesis; publisher Cool-down protected.
A context may need more containers than the whole-number quotient, or it may ask only for complete rows and leftover seats. A missing savings amount must be subtracted from the goal before dividing.
Teacher reviews the original open reasoning, diagrams, partner discussions and student-created word situations. First-party models are provided without copying publisher art.
Original source mathematical checkpoints: 378 = 4×94+2 (94 full boxes plus two unboxed, or 95 boxes if all must be boxed); 258 = 9×28+6; (1270−6)÷8=158; 711÷3=237; 3128÷8=391.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not the publisher's protected item): All 275 pupils need a seat on 8-seat buses. 275=8×34+3, so 35 buses are required.

KeyConcepts.Title: A remainder needs a contextual decision
KeyConcepts.Definition: For N objects and groups of size d, N=d×q+r with 0≤r<d.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use q complete groups when asking for full groups; use q+1 when every object must fit and r>0.
KeyConcepts.Example: 378 muffins: 94 full boxes and 2 muffins remain, but 95 boxes if all must be boxed.

KeyConcepts.Title: A short row is the remainder
KeyConcepts.Definition: A last partial row of seats does not count as a full row.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Divide total seats by row size; full rows are q and seats in the short row are r.
KeyConcepts.Example: 258 seats with 9 per full row: 28 full rows and 6 seats in the short row.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reconstruct a missing savings contribution
KeyConcepts.Definition: A school is still short by a certain amount after equal monthly contributions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Monthly saving = (goal − shortfall) ÷ months; verify months×saving + shortfall=goal.

WorkedExamples.Title: Muffins: 94 or 95 depends on the question
WorkedExamples.Question: There are 378 muffins and boxes hold 4 each. How many full boxes? How many boxes if all muffins must fit?
WorkedExamples.Method: Whole-number division, then interpret the two remaining muffins.
Steps: If two muffins may remain unboxed, 94 boxes are enough for the full boxes.
If every muffin must be in a box, use one more box: 95.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 94 full boxes and 2 leftover; 95 boxes if all muffins must be boxed.
WorkedExamples.Check: 94 × 4 = 376; the remaining 2 require another box if packing everything.

WorkedExamples.Title: Auditorium: full rows and a short row
WorkedExamples.Question: An auditorium has 258 seats in full rows of 9 and one shorter row. How many full rows, and how many seats in the short row?
WorkedExamples.Method: Interpret quotient as complete rows and remainder as seats in the incomplete row.
Steps: 29 full rows would require 261 seats, which is too many.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 28 full rows and 6 seats in the short row.

WorkedExamples.Title: Garden: reconstruct 8 equal monthly savings
WorkedExamples.Question: A school needs $1270. After saving equally for eight months, it is $6 short. How much did it save per month?
WorkedExamples.Method: Subtract the missing amount before dividing.
Steps: Multiply back and restore the missing six dollars.

WorkedExamples.Title: Creating a division situation: 711 ÷ 3
WorkedExamples.Question: Write a situation for 711 ÷ 3 and identify what the answer means.
WorkedExamples.Method: Invent equal groups and solve an exact whole-number division.
Steps: For example, 711 stickers are shared equally among three classes.
700 is not required; use partial quotients 600 ÷ 3=200 and 111 ÷ 3=37.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 237 stickers per class in this independent example.
WorkedExamples.Check: 3 × 237 = 711. Teacher checks students' own story meaning.

WorkedExamples.Title: Creating a division situation: 3128 ÷ 8
WorkedExamples.Question: Write a different situation for 3128 ÷ 8 and explain the quotient.
WorkedExamples.Method: Partition the dividend and interpret one of eight equal shares.
Steps: Suppose 3128 pencils are distributed equally among eight classrooms.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 391 pencils per classroom in this independent example.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Answering 94 boxes when every one of 378 muffins must be packed.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 94×4=376 leaves two muffins unboxed; the all-packed wording requires an additional box.
CommonMistakes.Correction: The exact all-packed answer is 95 boxes. If leftovers are explicitly allowed, 94 full boxes plus two muffins is valid.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 29 full rows would need 261 seats and the source asks for full rows plus a shorter row.
CommonMistakes.Correction: 28 full rows and a 6-seat short row.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dividing the $1270 target by eight instead of subtracting the $6 shortfall.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Eight equal monthly savings sum to $1264, not $1270.

SummaryPoints: Always interpret the quotient and remainder in the actual story.
378 muffins and boxes of 4: 94 full boxes plus 2, or 95 boxes when all muffins must fit.
258 seats, 9 per full row: 28 full rows and 6 seats in the short row.
Equal monthly savings: (1270−6)÷8=158. Student-written situations for 711÷3 and 3128÷8 require teacher review.
Edulytics independent Cool-down 275 pupils/8-seat buses: 35 buses, not the protected publisher item.
